claims.claim: scTab used donor-level splits by design (compromise between random and study holdout); corpus 22,189,056 cells, training split 15.2 M.
Testing scTab-corpus models on 21 newly added studies dropped macro-F1 from 80-84% to 52-57%.

Rejection can fail when a population is missing (Abdelaal); hierarchical rejection within datasets (Theunissen); conformal relies on exchangeability (Lopez-De-Castro); method certainties calibrated differently (popV); UQ on one lung atlas (Engelmann); selective classification definitions (Geifman); closed-set annotators match absent types to existing labels (Hu).
Simple baselines remain competitive with foundation models for annotation.
The CVID reference includes in-vitro activated PBMCs; Census disease field may hold multiple values under schema 2.4.0.
Validation-selected thresholds should be re-checked on each new study's labelled subset if one exists.
claims.limitations: Recommendation follows from measured transfer gaps; re-checking was not tested.
